user.title: MCP Domora
user.description:
Expose Home Assistant to MCP clients such as Claude, ChatGPT or an IDE assistant.

After setup, point your client at:

`{url}`

The client will ask you to sign in to Home Assistant and approve the connection. You can then choose which tools and which entities it may reach under **Configure**.

abort.single_instance_allowed: MCP Domora is already set up. Open its options to change what it exposes.

tool_groups.title: Tool groups
tool_groups.description: Switch whole capabilities on or off. Anything unchecked is not advertised to clients at all.

tools.title: Individual tools
tools.description: All {count} tools. Unchecked tools are hidden, even when their group is enabled.

entities.title: Entity exposure
entities.description: Which entities MCP clients may see and control. Leave a filter empty to apply no restriction. An entity listed under "always include" is exposed even if another filter would exclude it.

data.include_labels: Only entities with these labels (empty = all)

security.title: Security
security.description: Limits that apply to every client, on top of each user's own Home Assistant permissions.

data.read_only: Read-only mode (hide every tool that changes something)
data.allow_dangerous: Allow disruptive tools (restart, stop add-ons, write states directly)
data.require_admin: Only allow Home Assistant administrators to connect
data.allow_ha_tokens: Also accept long-lived access tokens instead of OAuth
data.max_results: Maximum items in a list response

clients.title: Connected clients
clients.description:
Clients that currently hold a token:

{clients}

Select any you want to disconnect. Revoking also removes the Home Assistant session behind it.

Server URL: `{url}`
